text:
2026-08-03 review, second half: Batch 3, Batch 4 and the A7 follow-up. Verification: 430 tests across 13 modules pass and scalafmtCheckAll is clean, up from 428 with the two new RED-first tests.

The A7 follow-up was the important part. A7 fixed one silently dropped codec field (JobObservation.reportedCluster), and the open question was whether that was an instance or a class. An exhaustive audit compared every hand-written encoder and decoder in AgentDomainJson, StructuredResultCodec, AgentMessageCodec, ControlCommandJson and JournalCodec against the fields of the type each serializes. It was an instance: no other hand-written codec drops a field. The mechanism that hid it is the general lesson and is now recorded on P6f.12, because a one-time audit cannot prevent the next defaulted field from going missing and only a round-trip law can.

The audit did surface four adjacent items, each verified against source rather than taken on report:
- P8.A14, fixed: both JobRef decoders validated a legacy `cluster` they then discarded, so a foreign or legacy payload could be rejected over a value nothing used. Worst on StructuredJson.decodeJob, which feeds the durable result decoders.
- P8.D8, filed: ResultContractDescriptor.maxBytes is read nowhere in main or test. The codec omission is a symptom; the field is publicly settable with no effect, so putting it on the wire would preserve a value that still does nothing. Needs a decision, not a codec patch.
- P8.A12, filed: ReportedState.truncated is dropped at SlurmParsers.scala:147-157 before any codec sees it, so a consumer cannot tell a complete flag list from a truncated one. No codec is at fault, which is why neither A7 nor codec ownership would have caught it.
- Examined and deliberately not filed: HandshakeResponse.maximumLogPageBytes does not round-trip None, because the decoder substitutes the frame-derived ceiling. Benign today and cross-guarded, since the only producer derives the value from the same frame the decoder sees and AgentService strips the PagedLogs feature when it is empty. Recorded here so it is not re-litigated as a defect.

Batch 3 resolved to less new work than expected, which is the correct outcome:
- The FrameDecoder quadratic accumulation is already named in P7.2, including the `buffered ++ input` line and a required before/after benchmark. Confirmed still live at FrameCodec.scala:40; no new scope.
- The base64 bounds asymmetry is now recorded on P6f.12 with exact lines: the remote path checks encoded length before allocating, while Decoder[BoundedEvidence] and Decoder[LogPage] decode straight into an unbounded array. Frame size is the only thing bounding them, so it is defence-in-depth, not a live overflow. resultRefs has no cardinality cap.
- P8.A15, fixed rather than deferred: the two ControlTransition throws needed no public shape change, so Phase D was the wrong home. ControlTransition now contains no throw and a new SchedulerQueryResult case is a compile error in one place instead of a runtime throw in two.

Batch 4 split cleanly into one thing that needed no evidence and three that did:
- P8.A13, fixed: MM:SS was not a corner case but what squeue prints for every sub-hour limit, so a 30-minute limit reported as Unknown. Fixed from documented output formats; no site capture needed.
- P8.G5, filed and blocked on a real transcript: a het component id like 12345+0 is ACCEPTED by JobId, because the identifier rules reject only whitespace and control characters. So it becomes JobRef("12345+0"), never matches the bound leader id, and the attempt takes the not-reported path. A silent no-match reported as "the scheduler did not report this job" is worse than a parse diagnostic, which is why this needs a capture before implementing.
- P8.A11, filed as a decision: `exit.forall(_.code == 0)` is true when nothing was reported, so a COMPLETED row with no exit code yields Completed(0), claiming a status the site never sent. Tied to the deferred P6f.32 partial-success design.
- P8.E1, filed with no prior owner: compact() trims only the in-memory event cache and the sole channel.truncate removes a torn tail, so the journal never shrinks and open replays every command ever issued. Startup cost grows forever and is paid exactly when recovering from a crash.

Housekeeping: removed modules/site, an untracked stale target/ from a module already deleted from build.sbt.
